item.description: A groundbreaking archaeological find at Tunnug 1 in southern Siberia unveiled cannabis seeds within a prince's tomb, dating back 2,800 years. This tomb is tied to intricate funerary rites, including horse sacrifices. item.title: Australia reverses military land sale plans after protests, saving four historic sites
item.description: The Australian government has opted to retain four significant historical military sites in public hands, responding to widespread public dissent against their potential sale. Notably, Victoria Barracks in Sydney and other sites in Victoria will remain untouched. The government aims to find new public purposes for these locations while preserving their heritage, and part of the broader reforms includes returning certain military lands to Indigenous communities. item.title: Tests on 8 frozen Inca mummies sacrificed show they had chewed coca leaves and had drunk alcohol
item.description: A remarkable archaeological find has revealed eight frozen mummies of children from the Inca Empire, believed to have been sacrificed. Analysis of their hair and nails showed they've ingested coca and alcohol, hinting at a diversity of ritual practices based on local customs. Notably, one mummy, Juanita, contained harmine traces, suggesting specialized ritualistic preparations. This research unveils a rich tapestry of ancient cultural traditions and ceremonies.
